newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses, still end lower.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses, still end lower.

text.p: Mexican stocks cut earlier losses at the close on Friday on pre-weekend buying but still finished lower, succumbing to Wall Street's undertow, traders said.
"Stocks bottomed out at the 3,660-point, which is where some local buyers stepped in. A rebound in the Dow also helped," said a trader at the Bancomer brokerage.

The leading IPC share index ended down 14.62 points, or 0.40 percent, at 3,680.56, but off a session low of 3,663.25. The Dow Jones meanwhile closed down 0.88 percent at 6,696.48 points, above a session low of 6,662.23.
Analysts said share prices fell due to a continued bout of profit-taking, as well as the adverse effect of Wall Street.
"It's the correction we had been expecting for days. It's very normal and healthy profit-taking," said Jaime Fernandez, an equity analyst at the Interacciones brokerage.
On the broad market, a total of 106 stocks changed hands, of which 55 declined while 29 finished ahead amid moderate trading volume of 76.3 million shares.
Retail stock Cifra A series headed the sliders' list, off 1.30 pesos at 9.60 pesos.
"Cifra A shares were traded at little volume. They're less liquid than other series and can be easily manipulated by small up- and downticks and small trades," a trader said.
Cifra was followed by holding company Accelsa, off nine centavos at 1.66 pesos.
"I would say Accelsa fell because it is infrequently traded and dealers finally decided to take profits on it," a dealer said.
Retail stock Ceramic ULD series gained 2.02 pesos to 12.00 to head the gainers' list, on what traders said was a favorable 1996 earnings report last week.
Dealers saw a rough ride for the bourse in the week ahead, with important U.S. economic data in the offing, such as advance Q4 GDP and existing homes.
"We still see the market sliding, on Monday at least, but we sould recover once the coast is clearer for U.S. financial markets," a broker said.
